summary: Cooley Hill fire tower in Easton, NH: built 1939 by CCC recruits, a 40-foot wooden tower later removed; a trail guide says remains are visible beside the Jericho Road Trail.

facts.status_note: A trail guide says the tower's remains can be seen beside the Jericho Road Trail; no other source describes the site.

access.note: Trails in the Cooley-Jericho Community Forest are multi-use; the Ammonoosuc Conservation Trust owns and manages the forest.

visit.trail_note: The Yellow Trail runs 3.1 miles to the summit from the Trumpet Round Road kiosk; the Jericho Road Trail reaches the tower site from NH Route 116.

events.note: Built by CCC recruits from Woodsville at Camp Wildwood, per a 1939 newspaper item and a trail guide

notes_for_editor: The 1939 build by CCC recruits rests on a 1939 Portsmouth Herald item quoted on Forest Lookouts and on a trail guide. Removal after about ten years and the remains beside the Jericho Road Trail rest on the trail guide alone. No staffing, fire or agency record was found in any fetched source. Search snippets about WWII women observers and a 1939-40 Forest Service tower list came from pages we could not open (NHDFL PDFs returned 403; firelookout.org cooley.htm returned 404), so they are left out. The trail guide places the summit near the White Mountain National Forest boundary, so the hill may be partly federal land; not confirmed. The removal date is unknown.
